notes.lr-necessary-assumption-knee-surgery-ana: Minor: (B) 'reports were honest' is a soft second candidate under negation (dishonest reports would also undercut the evidence). (D) is clearly the intended alternate-cause gap and is the better answer, but (B) is closer to defensible than a typical distractor; consider making (B) more obviously wrong (e.g., 'perfectly accurate in every case').
notes.lr-necessary-assumption-sarn-basin-ridge: Minor: (D) 'glacial movement never occurs without leaving deposits' is nearly a restatement of the stated premise 'Glaciers leave behind deposits,' so it reads as premise-restated rather than a clear wrong answer. (A) is the genuine gap (not found -> never present) and is the best answer; no change strictly required.
notes.lr-necessary-assumption-export-firms-wag: Minor: (B) and (D) are plausible-looking because the stimulus mixes a correlation with a causal mechanism; (E) is the only one that survives negation cleanly. Acceptable as a hard item, but note that the two-part evidence structure makes (D) feel more tempting than usual.
notes.lr-sufficient-assumption-ridgeline-docum: Minor: (E) (survey reliability) is a strong-looking competitor because the stimulus relies on survey data. (C) is the correct formal bridge (most viewers -> audience); (E) does not close that gap. Item is sound but (E) will draw many wrong answers.
